scenario: [RFCS.6.8]: the run identifier enters the hash as its UTF-8 bytes, not its code points. Here the engine is given run id `Zürich-run` (the `ü` is U+00FC, two bytes C3 BC in UTF-8) and tier id `edge` before it records ([RCTS.1.2.23]). LFST.2.2's session -- one Reading asserted, no pump -- is recorded: the assert's clock sample is the stream's first event, `ClockAdvance` at seq 0 ([LTIM.2.8.5], [LFST.7.1.3]), and the `FactAssert` follows it at seq 1. KNOWN ANSWER, computed from the clause's text with Python's `hashlib` in the build container, not by either runtime: r = 5ac3bc726963682d72756e; preimage `"ds.rfcs.event_id.v1"` 1F r 1F `edge` 1F be64(1) = 64732e726663732e6576656e745f69642e76311f5ac3bc726963682d72756e1f656467651f0000000000000001; SHA-256 = 717eaea5f801305302dc40a8822c3bfaaa60cd2e406d7740a5e3c68515863df0; byte 6 0x30 becomes (0x30 & 0x0F) | 0x80 = 0x80, byte 8 0x02 becomes (0x02 & 0x3F) | 0x80 = 0x82; so the event_id is 717eaea5-f801-8053-82dc-40a8822c3bfa. A derivation that hashed Latin-1, UTF-16 or one byte per code point records another id. `be64(seq)` is pinned below 2^32 only: a recording's `seq` counts every event from 0 ([LFST.7.1.3]), and no harness can reach 2^32 cheaply. PATH PINNED: the stamp on a recorded `FactAssert`, not a call to the helper ([STYL.5.10.8]) -- libds's `ds_rfcs_gen_event_id` (rfcs/codec.c) through pyds `Engine(run_id=, tier_id=)` and `Engine.record`, read back as each `FactAssert`'s message through libds's reader (`pyds.atoms`) in runner.py `_run_rfcs_roundtrip`; the Mercury runtime's `ds.rfcs.lfst_5_6_event_id` after `ds.engine.set_run_id` / `set_tier_id`, read back as `FactAssert` field 8 in compiler/mercury/test/test_behave.m `rfcs_roundtrip_result`.
